title: From Raw Documents to AI-Ready Data — Leo Platzer & Jeff Koss
talk_summary: A vendor demo (DZ Labs/Calibra) of a document-curation pipeline that tags, deduplicates, freshness-filters, and sensitivity-scans unstructured files before they enter a RAG/agent context store. The one genuinely transferable idea is generating a hierarchical 'context.md' index of folders/files so agents navigate by summary instead of reading raw files.

takeaways.technique: Folder-level context index (context.md) for agent navigation
takeaways.what_they_do: They generate a mirrored tree of markdown context files, one per folder, each stating document types, key topics, when to use the folder, and example questions, plus a top-level index, so the agent reads the index instead of opening individual files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your claw code for example or your codeex does not even have to look at the individual files to figure out what to look for but simply looks at the context MD file

takeaways.technique: Dedup + freshness filtering before context injection
takeaways.what_they_do: They measure duplication and staleness in the corpus and remove redundant or outdated documents from the knowledge base so top-K retrieval isn't filled with stale/conflicting content.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if your raw corpus ... 30% of your files are stale or duplicative, it can happen that up to 80% of your actual context your agent uses ... is filled up with stale information
takeaways.numbers: 30% stale/duplicate corpus -> up to 80% of used context stale; recall@1 roughly doubled; task completion +10-15% on multihop RAG eval

takeaways.technique: Evidence + confidence score attached to every AI classification
takeaways.what_they_do: Every AI-generated tag carries a pointer to the source passage and a model-reported confidence score, plus thumbs up/down few-shot feedback, so humans can audit why the model decided.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can see the evidence at the file level and the chunk level. I can see the confidence score

takeaways.technique: Pattern + LLM hybrid sensitivity scan with context
takeaways.what_they_do: They combine regex/pattern matching with LLM context to detect PII/PHI/IDs, letting the LLM propose regex syntax and locale-specific terms to cut false positives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: not only can we do AI based, we can do patternbased with context ... it's going to be less false positives as well
